author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution uses **depth-first search (DFS) with backtracking** to explore all possible finger movements while typing a word on a keyboard. It maintains the positions of both fingers (`left` and `right`) as it recursively processes each character, trying both options at each step: moving the left finger to the current character or moving the right finger. The `getMoveCost` function calculates the **Manhattan distance** between two keys using a coordinate map of the keyboard layout, and the algorithm tracks the minimum total cost across all possible combinations of finger movements.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution uses **dynamic programming** to efficiently find the minimum distance needed to type a word with two fingers. The `dp[i][j]` table stores the minimum cost to type the first `i` characters with one finger at letter `j`, while the other finger can be at any position. For each character, the algorithm considers two cases: keeping the previous finger at position `j` and moving the other finger to the current character, or moving the finger that was at `j` to the current character. The `getDistance` function computes **Manhattan distance** on the keyboard grid, treating each letter as a coordinate position (row and column).
